T: Increase the peace. Fire up the grill.
D: Three friends grow up in South Central Los Angeles, guided or lost depending on who's there for them.
P: Serve the mains at the backyard welcome-home barbecue.
S: the party when Doughboy gets out

Wings dried overnight, baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in a sticky barbecue, honey and hot sauce glaze. Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm barbecue sauce with honey and a splash of hot sauce, toss the wings through and serve with plenty of napkins.
Eggs boiled 10 minutes, yolks whipped with mayo, mustard, sweet relish and hot sauce, piped back, paprika on top.
Caramelised onion dip with ridged chips
the corner store down the street

Onions cooked slow until deep brown, folded through sour cream and cream cheese with chives and a dash of Worcestershire, served with ridged salted chips. Slice 3 brown onions thinly and cook in 30g butter and a splash of oil over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring, until deep brown. Cool completely. Beat 250g sour cream with 125g soft cream cheese, a dash of Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Fold in the onions and a handful of chopped chives. Chill for an hour and serve with ridged potato chips.
M: Pork ribs rubbed with paprika, brown sugar, garlic and cayenne, wrapped and baked at 150C for 2.5 hours, glazed with barbecue sauce over hot coals. Rub 2kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 2.5 hours. Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky. Serve with a crunchy cabbage coleslaw.

Chicken pieces brined in buttermilk, fried crisp in seasoned flour, served with baked mac and cheese and collard-style greens braised with smoked ham hock. Soak 1.5kg chicken pieces in 500ml buttermilk with salt and hot sauce overnight. Simmer a ham hock in 1L water for 1 hour, add 2 bunches shredded silverbeet and cook 20 minutes. Boil 300g macaroni, stir through 250g grated cheddar and 300ml milk and bake at 190C for 20 minutes. Dredge the chicken in 300g flour with paprika and garlic powder and fry at 165C for 12 to 14 minutes until 74C inside.
W: Roasted sweet potato mashed with butter, brown sugar, eggs, evaporated milk and spices, baked in a blind-baked case at 170C for 50 minutes.
K: Red fruit punch of cranberry juice, pineapple juice and lemonade, poured over ice from a big cooler.

s.note: the party when Doughboy gets out
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm barbecue sauce with honey and a splash of hot sauce, toss the wings through and serve with plenty of napkins.

Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, yellow mustard, a spoon of sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Serve chilled on the porch.

m.how: Rub 2kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 2.5 hours. Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky. Serve with a crunchy cabbage coleslaw.

w.how: Roast 800g sweet potatoes until soft, then mash with 60g butter, 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml evaporated milk, cinnamon and nutmeg. Pour into a blind-baked sweet shortcrust case and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until just set. Cool before slicing.

d.how: Fill a big drink cooler with ice. Pour in 1L cranberry juice and 1L pineapple juice and stir. Top up with 2L cold lemonade just before everyone arrives so it stays fizzy. Set out plastic cups and let people help themselves all afternoon.
